title: Last meeting with Oliver in 1928
summary: Oliver, stranded in Georgia, thanked Ory for the king title.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: That's what he told me. So I brought him 19... 27, 28. 28, that's about 28. He was stranded out in Georgia, you know.

And I left him and I was looking at my bar room. And he said, you owe me $100 for recording, you know. Tell me that happened to my man. And I said, all right. I said, you need any more money? He said, no. I need it, but you're too nice. You didn't protest me against the union. Uh-huh. I said, did you pay all the other guys? He said, yeah. I said, if you need anything, I said, I'll let you. He said, thanks for the name of the king. He shook hands.
Oh, yeah? Is that the last time you saw him? Uh-huh. That's the last time you saw him? Yeah. He said, me, that's a good.

And there wasn't George in there. He got stranded there. And the way he told me he saw him there. Uh-huh. The way he said, he said, I saw a little Joe. Someone told him he had a little fruit stand. He had two bananas and one potato. And he tapped him on me and said, I want a sack of potatoes. I said, what'd you do? Louie, huh?
